traits.label: Hymenium
traits.text: White to cream-colored pores that become grayish or brownish with age; may bruise dark brown.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Hymenium: White to cream-colored pores that become grayish or brownish with age; may bruise dark brown.

traits.label: Cap
traits.text: initially convex, becoming nearly flat with age; orange-red to orange-brown, dry, and slightly scaly.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Cap: initially convex, becoming nearly flat with age; orange-red to orange-brown, dry, and slightly scaly.

traits.label: Hymenium Attachment
traits.text: Attached directly to the stipe or slightly descending.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Hymenium Attachment: Attached directly to the stipe or slightly descending.

traits.label: Stipe
traits.text: 10-25 cm long, 2-4 cm thick; white, covered with small black scab-like scales.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Stipe: 10-25 cm long, 2-4 cm thick; white, covered with small black scab-like scales.

traits.label: Dimensions
traits.text: Cap: 8-20 cm in diameter.
traits.raw: 📐 Cap: 8-20 cm in diameter.

traits.label: Fruit body
traits.text: Fruit body: 18-45 cm tall.
traits.raw: 📏 Fruit body: 18-45 cm tall.

traits.label: Spore print
traits.text: Spore Print: Brown to olive-brown.
traits.raw: 🟤 Spore Print: Brown to olive-brown.

traits.label: Ecology
traits.text: Mycorrhizal, commonly found under birch trees.
traits.raw: 🌳 Mycorrhizal, commonly found under birch trees.

traits.label: Edibility
traits.text: Edible but should be cooked well; some people may experience gastrointestinal distress.
traits.raw: 🙂 Edible but should be cooked well; some people may experience gastrointestinal distress.

traits.label: Microscopy
traits.text: Spores 14-18 x 4-5 µm, fusiform (spindle-shaped).
traits.raw: 🔬 Spores 14-18 x 4-5 µm, fusiform (spindle-shaped).

traits.label: Odour
traits.text: Mild, not distinctive.
traits.raw: 👃 Mild, not distinctive.

traits.label: Overview
traits.text: Notable for its orange to orange-brown cap and the small black scales on its white stipe. It forms a symbiotic relationship with birch trees, although it may sometimes be found near other types of trees. The mushroom is edible but should be cooked thoroughly to avoid potential gastrointestinal issues.
